name: contact-v2
note: Every colour pair that actually occurs on /contact-v2, declared so it is enforced rather than assumed. Values transcribed from styles/tokens.css.

cotton.role: ground of sections 1 and 3; all text on noir

gray.role: secondary text on cotton — not used by this page

grayOnNoir.role: eyebrows, field labels, resting field rules on noir

cherry.role: the one solid field; accent text on cotton

maroon.role: hover/active depth step under cotton text

chili.role: graphic only on noir — seam, step numbers, invalid rule

paper.role: declared but deliberately unused by this page

contrastPairs.where: s1 eyebrow at 12px/500 — treated as normal above; listed to keep the pair explicit
s1 H1 at 42-104px; s3 email at 20-56px
s2 input values, step durations, fit statement, consent text, handover body, preview
s2 eyebrows, field labels 11-12px, responseStatement 15px, handover note 13px
resting 1px field rule, preview border, quiet-button rule
field error messages at 13px/500; invalid field label at 11-12px
the seam hairline, the 2px invalid rule, the 2px handover rule, the consent link underline
SEND INQUIRY / COPY INQUIRY label at 13px/600 on the cherry field
the same label during hover, active and pending
s3 email 2px underline; the global :focus-visible ring on cotton grounds
the focus ring on noir — this page's override of the global cherry ring
the check mark inside the consent box, which is a cotton field

mustFail.why: This is why the global :focus-visible cherry ring is overridden to cotton inside section 2. If this pair PASSES, the override is unnecessary and the spec should be revisited.
This is why body-size accent text on noir uses chili300, not chili. If it passes at normal size, DESIGN.md's red rule is wrong.
This is why the v1 paper form card reads as a printing artifact and why this page does not use paper.

Measured 1.26:1. Sections 1 and 3 therefore draw no hairline rules on cotton — the page separates blocks with space and with the noir band, not with a line nobody can see. Moved out of contrastPairs because the pair does not occur; a declared pair that never renders produces a false failure.
